BiblicalUsage: Firmness is the strength of the iron that stays in the clay. Nebuchadnezzar's image has feet of iron mixed with miry clay, a kingdom divided, yet there is in it of the strength of the iron — the firmness does not leave even when the mixture weakens it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that divided strength is still strength: the iron keeps its firmness in the clay, and the kingdom stands until God breaks it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
